statement: A researcher selected a random sample of $300$ adults from a list of all the adults who live in a certain town. Each adult in the sample reported whether they do a stretching routine every day and rated their own stress level. On average, the adults who stretch every day reported significantly lower stress levels than the adults who do not. Which conclusion is best supported by the study?

choices.text: Stretching every day causes lower stress for adults in the town.
choices.misconception: I thought a random sample was enough to show cause and effect, but each adult chose whether to stretch, so no one was randomly assigned to stretch.

choices.text: Stretching every day causes lower stress, but only for the $300$ adults in the sample.
choices.misconception: I mixed up random selection with random assignment. Random selection is what lets the result reach the whole town, and without random assignment the study cannot show cause and effect for anyone.

choices.text: The link between daily stretching and lower stress holds only for the $300$ adults in the sample, because the study is observational.
choices.misconception: I thought the results of an observational study can never be generalized, but the adults were randomly selected from the whole town, so the association can be generalized to the adults in the town.

choices.text: Among adults in the town, stretching every day is associated with lower stress, but the study does not show that stretching causes lower stress.

hints: Two questions matter: how were the people chosen, and who decided which adults stretch?
Random selection from a population supports generalizing to that population. Random assignment to groups supports a cause-and-effect conclusion. Check which of these the study used.
The adults were randomly selected from the town, but no one was randomly assigned to stretch: each adult made that choice.

solutions.reliable: Because the sample was selected at random from all the adults in the town, the result can be generalized to the town: among its adults, stretching every day is associated with lower stress. However, the researcher did not assign anyone to stretch. The adults chose for themselves, so those who stretch may differ from the others in other ways, such as having more free time, that could also explain their lower stress. Without random assignment, the study cannot show that stretching causes lower stress.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
